findings.text: The negative control is self-referential: planted = step["reference"] * (1 + 1e-10) and its distance from the reference is 1e-10 by construction, so `detected` can never be false and proves nothing about detecting a route defect; the manifest's negative_control_note describes a planted factor perturbation the code never performs.

_linear_problem re-implements the affine Newton operand assembly owned by nova/biot/magnetisation.py:1052-1116 rather than reusing an exported builder, so the refined reference can silently diverge from production if that construction changes; the brief forbade touching nova/, so a follow-up node should export a builder and have measure.py call it.

The fragment quotes the nearest route distance as 2.40e-13 while the resolvability check at measure.py:324 uses the minimum of each route's maximum of the two measures, which is 3.29e-13; both sit about three decades below the reference error so the verdict is unaffected, but the quoted number is not the one the code tested.
